title: Manage business information
goal: Every feed into the venture's records is running and current, every reader holds only the access the rule allows, and every stale feed, broken export and unused permission is named with its fix.

steps.do: Check each record type and feed against its freshness rule, list the records that are stale, the feeds that have written nothing since the last run and the fields that disagree between two systems, and put the list on the handoff with the date each was checked.

Repair what can be repaired without new access (rerun the export, refresh the sync, fix the field mapping), and record on each connection when it last ran, what it wrote and what it still cannot reach.

Read the access logs each connection exposes and compare who and which agent role actually read or wrote each kind of record this period with the rule for it, listing every read nobody expected and every permission nobody used, as the access-review skill sets out.

consider.why: An access rule nobody audits is a rule in writing only, and an unexpected read is the first sign of a leak.
consider.when: A connection exposes an access log, or the venture holds a customer's or an employee's personal data.

steps.do: Remove from each connection the read and write permissions the audit found unused, record the narrowed scope, and bring every request for wider access to the founder with the reason and the narrowest scope that would do.
Add each unrepaired feed and each unexpected read as evidence to the decision it bears on, and raise to the product lead the order of the fixes, worst exposure and most-used record first.

done_criteria.check: Does every feed say when it last ran and what it wrote, is every stale record either refreshed or named with its reason, and is every widening of access open as a decision rather than applied?
